Particípios fortes do grupo 1, passo a p: Strong participles, group 1, step by step
PASSO 1: os verbos FORTES (irregulares): STEP 1: STRONG (irregular) verbs form the Partizip II with «ge-» + stem + «-EN», not «-t». You already know the idea from English: "given", "eaten", "seen", "driven" — German keeps that -en ending on far more verbs. STEP 2: in GROUP 1, the stem vowel stays the SAME as in the infinitive: schlafen → geschlafen; laufen → gelaufen; fahren → gefahren; tragen → getragen; geben → gegeben (given); essen → gegessen (eaten); lesen → gelesen; sehen → gesehen (seen); kommen → gekommen (come). STEP 3: no umlaut in the participle: «du fährst», but «gefahren». STEP 4: careful: «fahren», «laufen» and «kommen» use «sein» in the Perfekt (see lesson 23); for now, just learn the participle. STEP 5: always learn the infinitive together with the participle — «sehen, gesehen» — the way you once learned "see, saw, seen".
o português também tem particípios irreg: English has exactly the same split: regular verbs take -ed ("played"), strong verbs take -en and often change the vowel ("given", "driven", "drunk"). German regular verbs take -t, strong verbs take -en. Many pairs even match: geben/given, essen/eaten, sehen/seen, kommen/come.
Strong verbs end in -en, like "eaten", not -t.
The participle of «essen» is «gegessen» (with an extra g).

Particípios fortes do grupo 2: a vogal m: Strong participles, group 2: the vowel changes
PASSO 1: no GRUPO 2, a vogal da raiz MUD: STEP 1: in GROUP 2, the stem vowel CHANGES in the participle, which still ends in «-en». STEP 2: the patterns are old Germanic ones that English shares: i → u (trinken → getrunken, like drink → drunk; finden → gefunden, find → found; singen → gesungen, sing → sung); ei → ie (schreiben → geschrieben, bleiben → geblieben); e → o (sprechen → gesprochen, like speak → spoken; helfen → geholfen; nehmen → genommen; treffen → getroffen; beginnen → begonnen, like begin → begun). STEP 3: «beginnen» has an inseparable prefix (be-): no «ge-» → begonnen. STEP 4: there's no absolute rule: use the patterns as a guide and memorize the pairs with the infinitive. STEP 5: all of these take «haben».
i → u in the participle, like drink → drunk.

PASSO 1: os verbos MISTOS têm a vogal di: STEP 1: MIXED verbs change the vowel (like strong verbs) but end in «-t» (like regular ones) — and English has the very same group: bringen → gebracht (bring → brought); denken → gedacht (think → thought); wissen → gewusst; kennen → gekannt. STEP 2: «haben» makes «gehabt» and «sein» makes «gewesen»; «tun» makes «getan» (done); «werden» makes «geworden» (with «sein»). STEP 3: with «sein» and «haben», conversation prefers the simple past (war, hatte), but the participle shows up in sentences like «Ich bin in Berlin gewesen» (I've been to Berlin). STEP 4: German has two verbs for "to know": «wissen» for facts («Ich habe das nicht gewusst» — I didn't know that) and «kennen» for people and places («Ich habe ihn gekannt» — I knew him).
